title: Security Criteria Declaration & Acceptance Framework for Private Deploy
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description:
This ticket establishes a declarative acceptance framework and endorsement checklist for security and compliance controls required for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to make acceptance criteria explicit for SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC role surfaces, immutable audit logging, and customer-managed key integrations (KMS/HSM), and to capture scope clarifications, trade-offs, and sign-off owners. This is part of the Private Deploy Security project and complements the operator runbooks and onboarding flow.

Background: Customers require a predictable, auditable onboarding path that demonstrates the Private control plane satisfies enterprise security requirements (federated identity, least-privilege access, encrypted key management, tamper-evident logs). Past ambiguities around which audit events are considered "sensitive" and whether KMS key rotation must be synchronous caused onboarding delays. This document clarifies those points and defines the acceptance flow for product, security, compliance, and operations teams to endorse readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Identity federation: End-to-end SAML 2.0 flow with Okta, OneLogin, or Azure AD validated against sample tenant (assertion acceptance, RelayState, signature verification).
SCIM provisioning: Create/update/deactivate users via SCIM v2; mapping documented and verified with two IdPs.
RBAC: Console and API enforcement of role matrix with at least four canonical roles (org-admin, infra-operator, app-developer, read-only). Role escalation attempts must be denied and logged.

KMS/HSM: Customer-managed key support for model artifact encryption and workspace secrets. Validate key wrap/unwrap across AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault; HSM flow smoke-tested in air-gapped environment.

Audit logs: All authn/authz events, KMS operations (wrap/unwrap requests), and admin actions are emitted to an append-only log store and exported to SIEM (Splunk/ELK) with preservation of event order and high-fidelity timestamps.

Log retention and redaction: Retention policy configurable per-customer; secrets and PHI redacted before export. Redaction must be reversible by operator only when approved in a documented escalation path.
Failure modes and fallback: If KMS vendor API is unavailable, operations should default to degraded mode but deny new key imports and surface explicit error codes to callers.
Upgrade/backwards compatibility: Private control plane upgrades must not change the RBAC schema in a way that silently escalates privileges; migration steps and dry-run telemetry are available.

decisions: Decision: Use SAML 2.0 as primary federated protocol for initial rollout; OIDC to be added in Q3 2025 as follow-up.
Decision: Support KMS key wrap/unwrap via vendor APIs rather than storing key material in control plane; HSM support provided via operator interface.
Decision: Audit retention default set to 1 year with the capability for enterprise customers to extend to 7 years behind a paid retention add-on.
